name: a silhouette's crystal bends a ray while a graph draws its maths
looks: A silhouetted figure holds up a small crystal. A thin bright ray travels in from off-frame and bends through it, tracing a sharp angle, while two plain labels sit fixed in the corners naming the two ideas in tension. Low in the frame a small sine-wave graph draws itself in sync with the ray's own progress.
build: The ray reveals with strokeDashoffset from source to crystal (power2.inOut); the bend triggers the instant the reveal reaches the crystal; the corner labels are static, low-contrast, present the whole beat; the graph's curve draws in lockstep with the ray's own timeline, same mechanic as physics-ray-diagram.
sound: A thin rising tone as the ray travels, a soft chime the instant it bends through the crystal.
prompt: Have a silhouetted figure hold up a small prop while a thin ray travels in and bends sharply through it, two one-word labels fixed in the corners naming the idea in tension, and a small graph drawing itself low in the frame exactly in step with the ray, so the demonstration and its maths read as one continuous move.
